final_answer: Ice floats on water due to the unique molecular structure of water. In liquid water, molecules are in constant motion, forming and breaking hydrogen bonds rapidly. When water freezes, the molecules arrange into a hexagonal crystalline lattice stabilized by hydrogen bonds. This structure creates open spaces between molecules, making ice less dense than liquid water. Because density decreases upon freezing, ice is buoyant and floats. This property is vital for ecosystems, as it insulates aquatic life beneath the ice. Safe.
